(4) UNRESOLVED — pre-registered unresolved; instrument said unresolved. 901 BAGBY ST, Houston (City Hall) -> no source to check: Houston is not in the ETJ register at all, so its ETJ is unmeasured.

contradicted.claim: The dispatch's own framing of falsifier 3 — 'Round Rock or Cedar Park (city-limits-only) ... Confirm your path returns an honest unresolved/absent-source disposition' — was implementable a simpler way, and I implemented it that simpler way first.
contradicted.whatTheEvidenceShowed: My first resolver earned `absent` from 'inside a published extent and inside no ring'. That returned a CONFIDENT ABSENT for a Round Rock address, because Austin's published extent is a loose rectangle covering Round Rock. A false negative dressed as a verified answer is exactly the defect class DEV_PROCESS forbids, and falsifier 3 caught it. Fixed by making the CONTAINING city's own register row decide the miss case: absent is earned only when that city is registered as publishing ETJ rings AND its rings were actually read.

fleetMemory.text: A PUBLISHER'S EXTENT IS NOT ITS BOUNDARY. Austin's published extent is a loose rectangle covering Round Rock, which publishes no ETJ layer at all. 'Inside the extent, outside every ring' therefore is NOT a verified absence — it is a false negative dressed as an answer, and it reads as confident to every downstream consumer. The miss case must be decided by the CONTAINING jurisdiction's own source row, not by the queried publisher's envelope. Pinned by a paired-control test.

AN EMPTY TABLE IS NOT AN ABSENCE when a register asserts rows should exist. tx_etj_source naming publishers with rings plus an empty tx_etj_boundary is an INCOMPLETE ACQUISITION and must answer unresolved; it is the single most likely state during a partial ingest, i.e. exactly when a wrong 'verified absent' would propagate fastest. Found by a test, not by review.

ETJ coverage in the wired footprint is close to universal (verified 2026-09-16): 20 of 23 cities publish a directly queryable ETJ layer; 5 carry city limits and ETJ in ONE layer separated by an attribute (Austin, New Braunfels, Kyle, Cibolo, Bastrop); Killeen's ETJ exists ONLY inside Belton's 17-city regional layer and Elgin's layer carries six Bastrop-county cities; only Round Rock, Cedar Park and Lockhart have no publicly queryable ETJ layer.
